# Quantum Deletion Capacity

This repository studies the entanglement-assisted capacity of ordered quantum deletion with hidden deleted positions and observable final length. All input carriers are charged. Preshared entanglement is unlimited; feedback, timing labels, free internal boundaries and a free classical message channel are absent.

## Read by question

- Scientific overview: README.md
- Definitions, assistance and half-diamond error: science/model.md
- Exact Kraus Gram blocks, scalar spectrum and mismatch-run bound: science/alignment-spectrum.md
- Finite-block coding, integer dimensions, iid limits and strong-converse scope: science/coding-theorems.md
- Physical interpretation and four-carrier example: science/interpretation.md
- Proof dependencies: science/README.md
- Prior results and precise attribution: references/RELATED_WORK.md
- Bibliographic records: references/references.bib
- Reproduction command and finite-check limits: verification/README.md

## Reader routes

- Story: README.md -> learning/bridge.md -> science/interpretation.md. Follow the missing-position question, the four-carrier example and the operational meaning of the rate penalty.
- Study: learning/README.md -> learning/anchor.md -> learning/milestones.md. The single educational anchor is Mark M. Wilde's Quantum Information Theory, with the source version and sections specified in anchor.md. The common map contains M01-M30 in background/preliminaries and narrative/innovation phases.
- Theorem: science/model.md -> science/alignment-spectrum.md -> science/coding-theorems.md. Keep normalized Choi operators, half-diamond error, squared-overlap entanglement fidelity and the arbitrary-encoder CP-order argument aligned.
- Reproduction: verification/README.md -> verification/run_all.py and verification/expected-results.json. Hosted mathematics has a separate source-to-rendered comparison described in verification/hosted/references/hosted-rendering.md; a numerical test or renderer pass is not a universal proof.

The leading small-deletion penalty is (p/2) log2(1/p) for fixed local dimension. The O(p) coefficient and exact general-p capacity are not determined. The strong converse is proved above the explicit upper threshold, not at an asserted exact capacity. A finite Gram computation does not prove the universal spectral or asymptotic statements. Codebook existence does not imply efficient decoding.
